chunks: Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

There was a man in earlier times who sought the world through halal means but could not attain it, and he sought it through haram means but could not attain it. Then al-Shaytan came to him and said: O this one, you have sought the world through halal and could not attain it, then you sought it through haram and could not attain it; shall I guide you to something by which you will increase your worldly gains and increase your followers? He said: Yes. He said: Invent a religion and call the people to it.

So he did so, and the people responded to him and obeyed him, and he gained from the world. Then he reflected and said: What have I done? I invented a religion and called the people to it, and I see no tawbah for myself except that I go to those whom I called and turn them away from it. So he began going to his companions who had answered him, saying: What I called you to is false, and I only invented it. But they began saying: You have lied; it is the truth, but you have doubted your religion and so turned back from it. When he saw that, he went to a chain and fixed for it a peg, then placed it around his neck and said: I will not remove it until Allah accepts my tawbah.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to a prophet from among the prophets: Say to so-and-so, by My Might and My Majesty, even if you were to call upon Me until your limbs are cut apart, I would not answer you until you bring back those who died upon what you called them to, so that they turn away from it.

key_terms.أَوْحَى: revealed, referring to Allah’s communication to a prophet
key_terms.أَوْصَالُكَ: your limbs or bodily joints, expressing extreme effort in supplication
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: Satan, who misleads the man into religious innovation
key_terms.بَاطِلٌ: falsehood, describing the invalid religion he had preached
key_terms.تَوْبَةً: repentance, which in this case requires remedying harm done to others
key_terms.حَرَامٍ: unlawful means that remain forbidden even when pursuing worldly gain
key_terms.حَلَالٍ: lawful means of seeking worldly livelihood
key_terms.دِينًا: a religion, here meaning a fabricated path invented by the man

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about inventing false religion and repentance for misleading others?
ai.summary: This hadith tells of a man who failed to gain worldly benefit through halal and haram means, then was misled by al-Shaytan into inventing a false religion to gather wealth and followers. When he repented, he learned that his repentance was not accepted unless those whom he had misled were restored, showing the grave consequence of corrupting religion and leading others astray.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4958 - Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdillah (as) who said:
"There was a man in earlier times who sought worldly gains through lawful means but could not attain them. Then he sought them through unlawful means, yet still could not attain them.
So, Satan came to him and said: 'O man, you have sought the world through lawful means and could not obtain it, and you sought it through unlawful means and still could not obtain it. Shall I guide you to something that will increase your worldly gains and followers?'
The man replied: 'Yes.'
Satan said: 'Invent a new religion and call people to it.'
So, the man did so, and the people responded to him and obeyed him, and he gained from the world.
Then he reflected and said: 'What have I done? I invented a religion and called people to it. I see no repentance for me except that I go to those I invited and turn them away from it.'
So, he began approaching his followers, saying: 'What I invited you to was false, and I only invented it.'
But they responded, 'You are lying! It is the truth, but you have doubted your religion and abandoned it.'
When he saw this, he took a chain, fixed it to a peg, placed it around his neck, and said: 'I will not release it until Allah (swt) accepts my repentance.'
Then Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to a prophet from among the prophets:
'Say to so-and-so: By My (swt) Might and My (swt) Majesty, even if you call upon Me (swt) until your limbs fall apart, I (swt) will not respond to you until you return those who died upon what you called them to and turn them away from it.'"
